name: Intune Hydration Kit
description: A PowerShell module that automates Microsoft Intune tenant setup by deploying 70+ security baselines, 43 dynamic groups, 24 device filters, compliance policies, app protection policies, and Conditional Access policies in a single command. Integrates OpenIntuneBaseline and supports multi-cloud environments.
keywords: how to configure new intune tenant
author: Jorge Suarez

securityCheck.aiSummary: Overall assessment: The IntuneHydrationKit codebase appears to be a structured Intune management toolkit with Graph API usage and Intune-centric features. While many patterns are standard for admin tooling, there are notable concerns: (1) dynamic loading of all scripts from Private/Public can enable unintended code execution if those directories are compromised; (2) a hard-coded default client ID could lead to insecure defaults and should be configurable; (3) runtime installation of modules from PSGallery introduces supply-chain risk and should be tightly controlled with signing/pinning; (4) in-memory token handling via ConvertTo-SecureString should avoid plain-text exposure; and (5) secret management for publishing (PSGallery API key) should be handled securely. No evidence of active credential harvesting, remote command execution beyond standard module installs, or explicit data exfiltration of user secrets was observed.
